# Qualification Requirements Quality Checklist: Windows Desktop Qualification

**Purpose**: Formal requirements-quality gate before `/speckit-tasks`. Areas: data safety, unsupported cases, external changes, Windows packaging and lifecycle, fair shell comparison, keyboard and visual behavior.
**Created**: 2026-09-29
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md), [plan.md](../plan.md), [research.md](../research.md), [data-model.md](../data-model.md), [quickstart.md](../quickstart.md), [contracts/operations.md](../contracts/operations.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

Audience: spec reviewer. The reviewer re-evaluated all items on 2026-09-29 after the Session 2026-09-29 decisions. Depth: formal gate before `/speckit-tasks`. Each finding evaluates the written artifacts only. No install, packaged run, fixture run, or measurement has run. "Decision needed" marks an undecided or conflicting requirement. "Satisfied" and "Implementation task" both mark a decided requirement. The build work for both goes to `/speckit-tasks`. "Implementation task" flags an item whose content is mainly a procedure to build or run. Neither class means done. "Covered by checklists/ux.md" marks an item that the reviewer evaluates in ux.md.

## Data safety

- [x] CHK001 Is "unchanged working-file bytes" defined by raw-content identity rather than timestamps or file size? [Clarity, Spec §FR-013, Constitution IV]
  - Finding: Satisfied — data-model §4 binds a raw-byte digest in `workingVersions`. data-model §4 makes timestamps and watcher events hints only. plan §Real-repository fixture matrix compares all fixture working-file bytes.
- [x] CHK002 Is repository state defined after a failed or interrupted hunk publication or commit, without an index rollback claim? [Coverage, Recovery, Spec §FR-015, §FR-020, §FR-023]
  - Finding: Satisfied — contract §4 "Hunk eligibility and publication" keeps the canonical index unpublished on a mismatch or unexpected candidate effect. research R4 "Outcome contract" and data-model §7 "State transitions" define commit outcomes and reconciliation. contract §8 defines the state after a restart.
- [x] CHK003 Is verification in real temporary repositories a stated requirement with a fixed assertion set, not only a test idea? [Measurability, Spec §FR-028, Constitution IV]
  - Finding: Implementation task — decided in FR-028 and plan §Real-repository fixture matrix (F01–F32, owned temporary root, full assertion set). It belongs in /speckit-tasks.
- [x] CHK004 Are stale-selection rejection criteria stated as a closed list of bound values and expiry events? [Completeness, Spec §FR-014]
  - Finding: Satisfied — contract §4 lists every value that a comparison binds. data-model §6 lists token expiry events. The contract §5 "Approval lifetime" row sets 60 seconds.
- [x] CHK005 Are the "ordinary Git EOL policies" enumerated (`core.autocrlf` values, `core.eol`, `text`/`eol` attributes, `core.safecrlf`)? Is hunk identity defined for mixed-EOL files and normalization-only differences? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-010, Assumptions]
  - Finding: Satisfied — FR-010 names `core.autocrlf`, `core.eol`, `core.safecrlf`, and the `text`, `eol`, and `crlf` attributes. FR-010 gives mixed files no hunk actions and normalization-only differences no hunk. contract §4 and data-model §5 refuse a hunk when `ls-files --eol` reports `mixed`. The spec edge cases and F04 cover `core.safecrlf` and each `core.autocrlf` value.
- [x] CHK006 Are index-entry flags classified for hunk actions: intent-to-add, assume-unchanged, and skip-worktree entries from sparse checkout without a sparse index? [Gap, Spec §FR-013, plan §Selected mutation protocols]
  - Finding: Satisfied — the spec edge cases give flagged entries Git status and no hunk actions. data-model §4 records the three flags, and data-model §5 sets reason `index-flag`. contract §4 rejects hunk requests for the three flags. research R3 "Publication protocol" step 10 verifies unrelated entries' flags. F10 includes a sparse checkout with a full index.

## Unsupported cases

- [x] CHK007 Does each excluded case have a defined user-visible behavior? Cases: binary, invalid UTF-8, oversized, rename, mode/type change, symlink, submodule gitlink, LFS, custom filter, encoding conversion, conflicts, and unfinished operations. [Completeness, Spec §FR-011, §FR-012, §FR-016]
  - Finding: Satisfied — FR-011 requires metadata, a specific limitation, and disabled actions. The plan state rows "Conflicted/unfinished operation", "Unsupported/binary", and "Limited output" define the visible states. data-model §5 "Support decision" lists the reason codes.
- [x] CHK008 Do unsupported repository forms have a defined user-visible behavior? Forms: bare repositories, a submodule checkout opened directly, a `.git` file with a missing target, and separate-git-dir layouts. [Coverage, Spec §FR-006, Gap]
  - Finding: Satisfied — FR-006 opens submodule checkouts and separate Git directories, and refuses bare and administration folders. data-model §2 and the contract §6 `repositoryDiscovery` context give `UNSUPPORTED_REPOSITORY` a remedy for each form. data-model §2 gives the missing-target remedy under `REPOSITORY_UNAVAILABLE`. The plan state row "Repository refused" defines the view. F07 and UI-10 cover each form.
- [x] CHK009 Is the user-visible behavior defined when Git refuses a repository for dubious ownership (`safe.directory`)? [Gap, Constitution V, Spec §FR-003]
  - Finding: Satisfied — the spec edge cases and the contract §6 `repositoryDiscovery` context define `DUBIOUS_OWNERSHIP`. The app shows the path and its own command with the contract §4 quoting. It never runs that command. It never offers Git's suggested command (research.md R5). contract §6 "Registration bootstrap" fixes the C locale. The plan state row "Repository refused" and F15 define the view and the test.
- [x] CHK010 Are Windows path cases addressed? Cases: paths longer than 260 characters (`core.longpaths`), case-only renames, and index entries that differ only by case. [Gap, Spec §FR-026]
  - Finding: Satisfied — the spec edge cases and data-model §5 refuse hunk actions with reason `path` for unreadable entries and case differences. F03 adds long-path, case-only-rename, and case-colliding fixtures. F03 never changes `core.longpaths`.
- [x] CHK011 Is display behavior defined for non-UTF-8 text: UTF-16 files, non-UTF-8 path bytes, and commit metadata in a legacy `i18n.commitEncoding`? [Coverage, Spec §FR-011, Edge Cases]
  - Finding: Satisfied — FR-008 shows invalid UTF-8 subjects and authors with replacement characters and an encoding label. The contract §3 "HistoryPage result" and data-model §4 "History page" rows carry the `encoding` header value. F19 tests a legacy `encoding` header. data-model §5 shows invalid path bytes as `\xNN` escapes. FR-011 keeps binary and invalid UTF-8 content, such as UTF-16, as unsupported comparisons. FR-019 refuses commits under a non-UTF-8 `i18n.commitEncoding`.
- [x] CHK012 Is the user-visible behavior defined when the package starts on an unqualified platform, such as Windows 10 or ARM64 emulation? [Gap, Spec §Scope Boundaries, §FR-029]
  - Finding: Satisfied — FR-029 and the Session 2026-09-29 answer run the package and show the label in two places. The places are the repository menu beside the selected Git version and the About window. plan §Provisional prerequisite admission and the plan repository menu paragraph show the label there. The plan About window Overview row also shows it. The contract §3 `getEnvironment` result reports the platform scope.
- [x] CHK013 Is untrusted inspection defined when a status read can run a filter process, such as LFS or custom clean filters? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-025, Contract §7]
  - Finding: Satisfied — FR-025 makes status reads wait for trust approval. contract §7 lists the keys that can fire for each read command. Repository-controlled keys (FR-025) block reads, and local and worktree keys always count as repository-controlled. System and global keys, such as Git LFS, run without approval when their program lies outside the repository. The plan state row "Trust required/changed" appears before the first status read. F17 tests an execution canary.

## External changes

- [x] CHK014 Is "external change" enumerated beyond working files, index, and references (HEAD target, attributes, configuration, trust, operation state, Git executable)? [Completeness, Spec §FR-022, §FR-014]
  - Finding: Satisfied — contract §4 binds each value. FR-014 revalidates them at each checkpoint. data-model §1 invalidates approval after executable replacement.
- [x] CHK015 Is behavior defined for a change during selection, during hunk staging, and during commit execution, not only between operations? [Coverage, Spec US3-9, US4-7, US4-8]
  - Finding: Satisfied — contract §8 invalidates approvals before replacement views arrive. FR-014 and research R3 "Publication protocol" cover pre- and post-publication changes. FR-018 and research R4 "Preflight and handoff" cover post-handoff changes.
- [x] CHK016 Is the consistency check defined that admits a mutation token after a Git read that spans an external change? [Ambiguity, data-model §4]
  - Finding: Satisfied — data-model §4 admits a token only after consistency checks. research R3 "Publication protocol" steps 5 and 11 revalidate under the owned lock and before publication. contract §4 and the contract "Commit validation and handoff" subsection apply the same rule to hunks and commits.
- [x] CHK017 Are detection timing and freshness bounds stated, including debounce, poll interval, and focus-return refresh? [Measurability, Spec §SC-007]
  - Finding: Satisfied — SC-007 sets two seconds for an idle foreground workspace. plan §Freshness and reconciliation sets a 100 ms debounce, a one-second foreground poll, and focus-return refresh.
- [x] CHK018 Is behavior defined when another Git process holds `index.lock`, including a stale lock that a crashed process left behind? [Coverage, Spec §FR-016, Edge Cases]
  - Finding: Satisfied — FR-016 shows the lock path and tells the user to remove the lock only after all Git tools stop. The plan "Error" state row shows the path with Copy path and Refresh for `LOCKED`. contract §8 treats every leftover lock as foreign after a restart. The contract §9 note sends Git-reported lock failures to a refresh, then to `LOCKED` with its path.
- [x] CHK019 Is suppression of obsolete read results defined with a stated identity rule? [Consistency, Spec US5-3, §FR-022]
  - Finding: Satisfied — contract §8 uses `repositoryGeneration` and `selectionId`. The contract §5 "Pending reads" row cancels superseded selection reads. plan §Freshness and reconciliation uses generation identifiers.

## Windows packaging and lifecycle

- [x] CHK020 Are the installer type and install scope decided with a source reference? [Completeness, Spec §FR-001, §FR-002]
  - Finding: Implementation task — decided in plan §Windows installation and native checks and research R7 (NSIS `currentUser`, LocalAppData, no elevation); belongs in /speckit-tasks.
- [x] CHK021 Is the WebView2 runtime mode decided, with a native check that runs before webview creation? [Completeness, Spec US1-2, §FR-002]
  - Finding: Implementation task — decided in research R7 "Windows distribution decision" (`webviewInstallMode: skip`, preinstalled runtime) and contract §7; belongs in /speckit-tasks.
- [x] CHK022 Is Bun service bundling decided: sidecar path, compile flags, startup directory, and environment sanitation? [Completeness, Constitution II, Constitution V]
  - Finding: Implementation task — decided in quickstart §2, research R7 "Compiled-service hardening", and contract §7; belongs in /speckit-tasks.
- [x] CHK023 Is service crash behavior defined, including automatic restart, a restart limit, and the visible state? Is WebView2 renderer-process failure covered? [Coverage, Recovery, Spec §FR-023]
  - Finding: Satisfied — FR-023 forbids automatic restart, so a restart limit is moot. The plan "Component stopped" row offers a restart action for the service, renderer, and browser process. plan §Service and native shell subscribes to WebView2 `ProcessFailed`. FR-023, plan §Service and native shell, and contract §8 block mutations after a service restart until an explicit refresh.
- [x] CHK024 Is orphan prevention after a shell crash stated for the service Job? Is recovery defined for an owned index lock or candidate file that a crash leaves behind? [Completeness, Spec §SC-008, plan F14]
  - Finding: Satisfied — contract §6 "Process fields" gives the service Job and each operation Job kill-on-close and no breakaway. contract §8 treats leftover locks and candidate files as foreign and names candidates with `arbareto-candidate-`. FR-016 and the plan "Error" state row give the lock guidance. F14 tests the shell crash.
- [x] CHK025 Is single-instance behavior decided? [Gap, plan §Service and native shell]
  - Finding: Satisfied — plan §Service and native shell allows more than one instance. Each instance treats the others as external writers. Native settings use whole-file replacement, and the last writer wins. A named mutex per common directory excludes mutations across instances (FR-015, contract §6, 2026-10-01). The quickstart §6 scenario tests two instances on one repository and on linked worktrees. Scope: the `Local\` mutex covers one logon session, and FR-015 states this scope. Instances in two sessions rely on `index.lock` only (contract §6 "Cross-instance exclusion").
- [x] CHK026 Are upgrade-in-place, uninstall, and reinstall defined, including which data stays: native settings, the WebView2 user-data directory, and any persisted logs? [Gap, plan §Windows installation and native checks, quickstart §3]
  - Finding: Satisfied — plan §Windows installation and native checks keeps native settings and webview data on upgrade and uninstall. The Delete app data option removes both folders. The plan section and contract §7 write no log files and keep logs in memory. data-model §1 uses documented defaults for unknown settings, with no migration. quickstart §3 step 8 tests each case.
- [x] CHK027 Is code signing deferred with a reason? Is the SmartScreen and Mark-of-the-Web behavior for the unsigned local installer addressed? [Completeness, Spec §FR-033, §SC-011]
  - Finding: Satisfied — FR-033 and research R7 "Signing and deferred authenticated updates" defer signing to the public-release gate. plan §Windows installation and native checks expects the SmartScreen prompt and records a policy block as an environment limitation. quickstart §3 step 1 specifies a Zone.Identifier record and Internet-zone and unmarked cases.

## Fair shell comparison

- [x] CHK028 Is the comparison target stated, given that Electrobun implementation is out of scope? [Clarity, Spec §FR-031, research R1, R8]
  - Finding: Satisfied — plan §Matched-condition comparisons makes Git Extensions `7.2.1.7` a matched product baseline. The same section gives Electrobun no packaged measurement and scopes "both candidates" to a future approved comparison.
- [x] CHK029 Are hardware, fixtures, build configuration, cold and warm state, run counts, and statistics fixed before measurement? [Measurability, Spec §FR-030, §SC-006, Constitution VII]
  - Finding: Implementation task — decided in plan §Fixed release-build measurement protocol; belongs in /speckit-tasks. It fixes hardware, M, L, and W-M fixtures, seed, reboots, run counts, warm-up runs, p95, capture source, and bootstrap interval.
- [x] CHK030 Are budgets and pass/fail rules stated per metric, with a rule for metrics that have no budget? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §SC-005–SC-008]
  - Finding: Satisfied — plan §Measurements and budgets sets a statistic and a budget per metric and marks report-only metrics. FR-032 keeps a missed budget a failure unless a trade-off approves a new target.
- [x] CHK031 Is the decision role of the Git Extensions baseline stated? [Ambiguity, Spec §SC-010, §FR-031]
  - Finding: Satisfied — FR-032 limits Git Extensions results to the SC-015 comparison targets. The plan §Matched-condition comparisons section defines the conditions, end-frame content, run counts, ratio and interval rule, and miss attribution.
- [x] CHK032 Is the evidence location stated, with a record format for failures, causes, and attempted remedies? [Traceability, Spec §FR-032]
  - Finding: Satisfied — FR-032, plan §Hard blockers and evidence rules, data-model §8, and quickstart §11 keep records in research.md. The records hold the required fields.
- [x] CHK033 Are the trigger conditions for considering another shell defined, including which gate failures count as shell-attributable? [Clarity, Spec §FR-032, Constitution VIII]
  - Finding: Satisfied — plan §Hard blockers and evidence rules defines a shell-attributable failure by three tests. Only a shell-attributable B-WINDOWS or B-PERFORMANCE failure triggers a shell review. The same section defines a reasonable remedy and the remedy kinds to record. FR-032 requires the attribution rule.

## Keyboard and visual behavior

- [x] CHK034 Are keyboard bindings, focus restoration after dialogs, forced colors, DPI profiles, per-monitor scaling, reduced motion, and About window access covered? [Traceability, checklists/ux.md]
  - Finding: Covered by checklists/ux.md — CHK006 (profiles), CHK007 (DPI changes), CHK008 (per-monitor scaling), CHK016 and CHK017 (forced colors). Also CHK018 (reduced motion), CHK019 (bindings), CHK021 (focus restoration), and CHK047 (About access). All nine are `[x]`, and their current text covers the question.
- [x] CHK035 Do busy and cancel states have a stated keyboard path to the Cancel control in the status region? [Coverage, Spec §FR-021, §FR-005]
  - Finding: Satisfied — plan §Keyboard and focus makes Tab and Shift+Tab reach every action. That includes Cancel in the status region of plan §Two feasible layouts, layout A. The plan "Busy" state row keeps cancellation available. F6 moves only among the list, comparison or inspector, and composer.
- [x] CHK036 Is focus behavior defined when the focused control becomes disabled by a busy, stale, or blocked state? [Gap, Spec §FR-005, §FR-021]
  - Finding: Satisfied — FR-005 forbids state changes to remove focus from a control that becomes unavailable. plan §Compact token system uses Base UI `focusableWhenDisabled`. The plan §Keyboard and focus "Unavailable control" row keeps the four mutation controls focusable when disabled. The visible reason is the accessible description.
- [x] CHK037 Are WebView2 browser accelerators and page zoom defined, such as Ctrl+R, Ctrl+F, Ctrl+P, Ctrl+plus, Ctrl+wheel, Alt+Left, and developer tools? [Gap, Spec §FR-004]
  - Finding: Satisfied — plan §Keyboard and focus disables browser accelerator keys through `with_webview` and keeps `zoomHotkeysEnabled: false` at 100% zoom. Release builds omit developer tools. The "Refresh" row keeps F5 as a bounded refresh. quickstart §7 verifies each listed key and records pinch zoom.
- [x] CHK038 Does the spec state screen-reader requirements with pass criteria for accessible names and live announcements? [Consistency, Spec §FR-005, Constitution VII]
  - Finding: Satisfied — the reviewer accepts the explicit deferral: the Session 2026-09-29 Narrator answer and spec Scope Boundaries. Also plan §Screenshot review during implementation, quickstart §7, and research R10.
- [x] CHK039 Is the focus target defined after the native close-during-mutation prompt and after a successful commit clears the tray? [Coverage, Spec §FR-024, §FR-034]
  - Finding: Satisfied — the plan "Close during mutation" state row returns focus to the last logical focus target after Stay open. plan §Keyboard and focus focuses the message field after a reconciled intended success in Changes. In History, focus stays unchanged.

## Cross-area consistency

- [x] CHK040 Is the prerequisite minimum-version admission consistent with self-updating prerequisites, such as Evergreen WebView2 and Git for Windows updates? [Conflict, plan §Provisional prerequisite admission, research R7]
  - Finding: Satisfied — plan §Provisional prerequisite admission keeps the clean-install environment offline after prerequisite installation. The reference host records Git and WebView2 versions before and after each series. A version change voids the series until the series repeats with the new recorded version. The quickstart §10 procedure stops the series on a change.

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Add comments or findings inline
- Link to relevant resources or documentation
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
- "Decision needed" items are candidates for `/speckit-clarify` or a plan update. Build work for "Satisfied" and "Implementation task" items goes to `/speckit-tasks`.
